articles.title: Trump walking into Xi and Putin's trap as 'terrified' allies fear concessions: WSJ
articles.description: U.S. allies are increasingly anxious about President Donald Trump’s Shenzhen summit with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin, warned the Wall Street Journal editorial board. In an editorial titled “Trump Meets With the Anti-U.S. Axis,” the board wrote that the meeting was stirring more unease among allies than among adversaries. It wrote that allies in tough neighborhoods were “terrified” of what Trump might concede. Trump said nuclear weapons would be a focus, and the board wrote that Ukraine, Iran and trade could also arise. The board gave Trump credit on nuclear policy, citing his long-standing aversion to the bomb, the expiration of New START and the exposure of secret Chinese nuclear testing. But it wrote that the trust needed for real arms control was missing amid the China-Russia-Iran-North Korea axis, and that Trump hadn’t built leverage through a military buildup like Ronald Reagan’s. It wrote that Xi wouldn’t discuss nuclear weapons until he bargained from parity or better. "The real risk is that Messrs. Xi and Putin can hide behind nuclear talks — only responsible actors working together here — and move on what they really want. That’s to give the world the impression that the three men control the world’s fate in something resembling a second Yalta conference," wrote the board. It warned that any trilateral plan on Ukraine would be a mistake and asked whether the administration would negotiate over Europe’s head. It wrote that Xi would watch whether the free world gave up on Ukraine to gauge his chances on Taiwan. The board wrote that Trump could press Xi and Putin to stop aiding Iran but had dismissed their help to Tehran. It added that Trump would have more leverage in Washington, pushing his $1.5 trillion defense budget through the defeated GOP Congress. "The best outcome of the trilateral summit would be nothing — handshakes, perhaps a chat about extending the trade truce with Beijing beyond January. But these summits come with compounding costs when Mr. Trump frightens allies over and over again for no outcome," the board wrote, concluding, "If Mr. Trump wants to be a peacemaker, he has to accept that he’s President at the dawn of a coordinated and hostile challenge to U.S. interests, and Messrs. Xi and Putin are running it."
